pageCache.pageTitle: Headteacher’s Welcome — St Mary & All Saints
pageCache.text:
Headteacher’s Welcome
Letting our light shine and making a difference in everything we do.
Welcome to St Mary & All Saints
A very warm welcome to St Mary & All Saints Church of England Primary School.
This is a special place where children receive a first-class education while developing the character, confidence, and resilience needed to succeed in today’s modern world.
Whether you are a prospective parent choosing the right school for your child, a current family checking in, or a visitor wanting to learn more about our vibrant community, we are delighted that you are here.
Our vision statement is simple yet powerful: “Let our Light Shine, Make a Difference.”
Growing the Whole Child First
Rooted in our proud Christian ethos, we believe passionately in growing the whole child first. We want all of our pupils to feel secure in who they are, to discover their unique passions, and to let their individual lights shine brightly.
But we also teach our children the importance of looking outward. Thinking of others and being a positive force in society is at the very heart of our school community, and our pupils take great pride in making a meaningful difference both inside and outside the classroom.
Our Core Values
Our daily life is underpinned by four core values that guide our pupils every day:
Respect: Understanding that everyone deserves to be treated as we would wish to be treated ourselves.
Resilience: Trying our absolute best, working hard, and learning from our mistakes.
Kindness: Treating everyone we meet with care, recognising that everyone is equal.
Curiosity: Staying eager to learn, asking big questions, and exploring the world around us.
Experience St Mary & All Saints
Please explore our website to find out more about our community, but more importantly, come and see us in action. This is a nurturing place where your child will be welcomed, celebrated, and supported to grow.
If you are considering joining our school family, we would love to show you around during a working school day so you can feel the warmth and energy of our classrooms firsthand. Please contact our school office to arrange a visit—I look forward to meeting you!
To read more about our Church of England heritage, parish links, and inclusive family ethos, please visit our Our Ethos & Christian Distinctiveness Page.

pageCache.pageTitle: Google Classroom — St Mary & All Saints
pageCache.text:
Google
Classroom
Click here to login to Google Classroom
Quick Student Login
Pupils can securely access their virtual classrooms on any desktop computer, laptop, tablet, or smartphone.
Click the direct login link below.
Log in using your school Google username (e.g., username@stmaryallsaints.co.uk) and your secure password.
Select your current class card from the home dashboard to view your latest assignments.
Log In to Google Classroom (External Link)
Information for Parents & Guardians
We warmly encourage parents to check Google Classroom together with their children. Inside the platform, you will find:
The Stream: A live feed of class announcements, weekly updates, and reminders from your child's class teacher.
Classwork Page: The structured area where weekly homework projects, spelling lists, and learning materials are clearly organized by topic or week.
Upcoming Tasks Box: A handy widget on the left side of the screen that highlights any homework tasks approaching their due date.
Google Classroom Hub
At St Mary & All Saints, we harness digital technology to expand our pupils' Curiosity and foster independent learning. Google Classroom is our secure online learning platform where teachers share homework, digital resources, and interactive class updates.
Whether your child is completing a weekly homework task or accessing home-learning resources, this hub is designed to make digital learning safe, supportive, and seamless.
Google Chrome
In order to use Google classrooms on a computer, you will need Google Chrome as your internet browser. To install this, click on the icon above which takes you to a download button. Click download and follow the instructions in the installer.
Google Classroom
Click the button to go to your child’s class page. You will need to log in with their e-mail and password. If you have misplaced these details, please contact the school and we will support you with this.
The Classroom App
The easiest way to use Google classroom is through the app. The Classroom app can be downloaded on Android (Android refers to most non-Apple mobile phones and tablets), Apple® iPhone® or iPad®, or mobile devices running Chrome OS to manage your class and get work done.
Android
To use Classroom on your Android device, download the Classroom app from Google Play.On your device, tap Play Store.Find and install the Google Classroom app.
iPhone and iPad
To use Classroom on your iPhone or iPad, download the Classroom app from the Apple® App Store®.On your device, tap App Store.Find and install the Google Classroom app.
FAQs
Lost or forgotten passwords
Contact School Office
For data security and safeguarding reasons, class teachers cannot reset passwords directly. If your child has forgotten their login details, please email the main school office at office@stmaryallsaints.co.uk and our technical team will securely reissue them.
Using tablets and smartphones
If you are accessing the platform via an iPad, Android tablet, or mobile phone, we highly recommend downloading the free Google Classroom App from the Apple App Store or Google Play Store rather than using a mobile web browser. It provides a vastly superior, child-friendly user experience. Please see above for links
The 'Permission Needed' error
Check Active Accounts.
If you see an error message stating you do not have permission to view a page, it usually means a personal or parental Gmail account is logged into your web browser. Ensure you log completely out of personal accounts, or open a private 'Incognito' window, before entering your child's official school login credentials

Let Your Light Shine: Build your future in a nurturing community.
Work With Us: Vacancies & Careers
Thank you for your interest in joining the team at St Mary & All Saints CE Primary School. We are an ambitious, nurturing, and inclusive community dedicated to helping both our pupils and our staff let their unique lights shine.
When you work with us, you join a supportive environment where professional development is valued, and every colleague is empowered to make a meaningful difference.
Current Vacancies
We do not currently have any active staff or governor vacancies at this time.
However, we are always keen to connect with passionate teachers, dedicated learning support assistants, and skilled operational staff. We warmly invite you to join our Talent Pool so we can contact you as soon as a suitable position opens up.
Join Our Talent Pool
If you would like to build your career at St Mary & All Saints in the future, we are always keen to connect with talented educators and support staff for future opportunities
Equality, Diversity & Inclusion (EDI)
At St Mary & All Saints, we believe in diversity of thought and actively welcome individuals from all backgrounds to bring their valuable skills to our community. We are an equal-opportunities employer committed to creating a diverse workforce where everyone can contribute to their fullest potential with dignity, comfort, and independence.
Disability Confident Employer: As a Disability Confident organisation, we guarantee an interview for all candidates with disabilities (as defined by the Equality Act 2010) who meet the minimum criteria for any advertised post.
Reasonable Adjustments: We are completely open to accommodation requests regarding assistive technologies, accessibility tools, or any other reasonable adjustments.
If you require any support or adjustments to assist you through our application or recruitment processes, please contact our school office in complete confidence via office@stmaryallsaints.co.uk
Safeguarding & Child Protection
St Mary & All Saints CE Primary School is strictly committed to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of children and young people. We expect all staff, volunteers, and governors to share this unwavering commitment.
All successful future applicants will be required to undergo rigorous child protection screening appropriate to the post. This includes comprehensive checks with past employers, online safer-recruitment vetting, and an enhanced check via the Disclosure and Barring Service (DBS).

pageCache.pageTitle: SEND & Inclusion — St Mary & All Saints
pageCache.text:
SEND & Inclusion
Letting our light shine and making a difference in everything we do.
SEND & Inclusion: Flourishing Together
At St Mary & All Saints, our staff and governors are passionate about ensuring a high-quality, inspiring education for every single child. We are fully committed to meeting the diverse educational needs of all our pupils, providing exciting and accessible experiences that allow them to grow and let their unique lights shine.
We believe that true inclusion is a living expression of our value of Respect—recognising that every child is equal, valued, and capable of making a meaningful difference.
Early Identification & Personalised Learning
We closely track the progress of every individual child using regular termly assessments, expert teacher insights, and specialised resources to identify any specific learning or developmental needs as early as possible.
When pupils face unique barriers to learning, we design tailored, high-quality interventions to help them overcome these challenges. This personalised approach applies across the entire academic spectrum, ensuring we nurture both our pupils with Special Educational Needs and Disabilities (SEND) and those who are identified as academically more able.
Our Graduated Approach
Where a child is identified as having a particular learning, physical, or behavioural need, we put tailored strategies into place following the Bucks Graduated Approach Model.
To ensure our support is dynamic and effective, we use the Assess, Plan, Do, Review cycle:
Assess: We identify specific barriers to learning.
Plan: With great Kindness and care, map out exact targets.
Do: We deliver targeted classroom support or specialised interventions, building the child's Resilience and confidence.
Review: We regularly evaluate progress alongside parents and the child to ensure the support is working.
To provide the highest level of expertise, we work closely with external agencies, including the Specialist Teacher Service, Occupational Therapy (OT), Speech and Language Therapy (SLT), and our attached school Educational Psychologist (EP).
Partnering with Families
We believe that parents and carers are vital partners. You will be involved right from the outset and kept fully informed of your child’s progress through regular meetings.
If a child requires a SEND Support Plan (SSP) or an Education, Health and Care Plan (EHCP), these are always co-written in close, warm collaboration with the family and the child, ensuring everyone works together towards the same ambitious goals.
Local Support and Advice
Bucks SENDIAS Service: Provides free, confidential, and impartial information, advice, and support on all matters relating to SEND for children and young people aged 0 to 25 and their families.
Online:Contact the SENDIAS Service
Email: sendias@buckinghamshire.gov.uk | Telephone: 01296 383 754
Buckinghamshire Local Offer: For comprehensive information about local SEND services, explore the Buckinghamshire Family Information Service.
Get in Touch
If you have any questions or would like to discuss your child's specific needs, our team is always here to support you with an open door and a listening ear. Please contact the school office, who will gladly pass your details to Mrs Levin, our Assistant Head for Inclusion.
Email: office@stmaryallsaints.co.uk
Telephone: 01494 673762
For a comprehensive look at our statutory provisions, please view our full SEND Policy and SEN Information Report on our Policies Page.

Sports Premium
Letting our light shine and making a difference in everything we do.
Sports Premium
At St Mary & All Saints, we believe that staying active is essential for a child’s development, happiness, and well-being.
The Primary PE and Sport Premium is government funding allocated directly to primary schools across England to improve physical education and sports. This funding helps us give our children an active start to life, boosting both their physical and mental health, while supporting positive behavior and academic success.
Our Key Objectives
This funding is ring-fenced, meaning it can only be spent on physical education and sports provision. We use it to achieve five key goals:
Daily Activity: Engage all pupils in regular physical activity and healthy habits throughout the school day.
School Culture: Raise the profile of PE and sport across the entire school to drive overall school improvement.
Confident Staff: Build the skills, knowledge, and confidence of our teachers and staff to deliver exceptional PE lessons.
Varied Experiences: Offer a broader, more exciting range of sports and physical activities to all pupils.
Competitive Sport: Increase opportunities for our children to take part in competitive sports and tournaments.
How We Invest the Funding
We focus on making sustainable improvements that will benefit our current pupils and leave a lasting legacy for future year groups. The premium is used to:
Introduce new, exciting sports and activities to make PE lessons enjoyable for everyone.
Provide professional development, expert coaching, and high-quality training resources for our teaching staff.
Invest in new, updated sports equipment for lessons and playtime.
Run and maintain a vibrant variety of after-school sports clubs.
Embed physical activity into the structure of the standard school day.
The Positive Impact on Our Pupils
Staying active does more than just build physical fitness. We see firsthand how this funding transforms our school community by:
Building Friendships: Strengthening peer relationships through team sports, collaboration, and clubs.
Reducing Stress: Boosting physical fitness while lowering anxiety and stress levels.
Inclusivity: Empowering children who might normally distance themselves from sports, giving them the confidence to try new activities and feel deeply valued.
Strategy Documents & Accountability Reports
We carefully track and report our sports premium spending to ensure maximum impact. You can download our full allocation details, spending plans, and impact reports below:

pageCache.pageTitle: Pupil Premium — St Mary & All Saints
pageCache.text:
Pupil Premium
Letting our light shine and making a difference in everything we do.
Pupil Premium
At St Mary & All Saints, we want every single child to "let their light shine" and reach their full potential.
Pupil Premium is extra funding provided by the government to help schools support children and ensure they have the same opportunities to succeed as their peers, regardless of their background or family circumstances.
Does My Child Qualify?
The school receives this extra funding for any pupil from Reception to Year 6 who falls into one of the categories below.
1. Free School Meals (Income-Related)
This is the most common reason children receive Pupil Premium. Your child may be eligible if you receive any of the following benefits:
Income-based Jobseeker’s Allowance
Child Tax Credit (provided you do not also receive Working Tax Credit and have an annual income under £16,190)
Support under Part VI of the Immigration and Asylum Act 1999
The Guarantee element of State Pension Credit
Important Note for Reception, Year 1, and Year 2 Parents: While your child automatically receives a free lunch under the government's Universal Infant Free School Meals scheme, it is still vital that you apply for Pupil Premium if you meet the criteria above. Registering ensures our school receives this valuable extra funding to support your child's learning, and guarantees they will continue to receive free meals when they transition into Key Stage 2 (Year 3 and above).
2. Looked After and Previously Looked After Children
Children who have been in local authority care for one day or more.
Children who have left local authority care due to adoption, a special guardianship order, a child arrangement order, or a residence order.
3. Service Children
Children of armed service personnel are eligible if:
One of their parents is currently serving in the regular armed forces.
One of their parents served in the regular armed forces in the last 3 years.
One of their parents died while serving, and the pupil receives a pension under the Armed Forces Compensation Scheme or War Pensions Scheme.
How We Use the Funding
The government allows school leaders to decide how best to spend this money, as we are closest to our pupils and understand their daily needs. We follow a proven, three-part approach to get the absolute best results for our pupils:
Excellent Teaching: Investing in high-quality training and resources to ensure daily classroom learning is outstanding for everyone.
Targeted Support: Providing extra help, such as small group work, 1-to-1 reading support, or specialized resources for children who need a boost.
Wider Strategies: Helping with the broader aspects of school life, such as supporting the cost of school trips, clubs, and emotional well-being.
Please note: This funding is not locked to individual children. Instead, we pool the resources to fund projects, staff, and equipment that best support the entire group of eligible pupils.
How to Apply (Completely Confidential)
Applying is quick, simple, and entirely confidential. Other families and children will not know who receives this support.
If you believe your child meets any of the criteria above, please collect an application form from the school office, fill it out, and return it to us as soon as possible.
Our Strategy & Reports
To see exactly how we plan to use this year's funding and review our past successes, you can download our strategy documents below:
Pupil Premium Strategy 2025-26 Autumn
Pupil Premium Strategy Report Acronyms Guide
Link: Government Guide to Pupil Premium

Letting our light shine and making a difference in everything we do.

Letting our light shine and making a difference in everything we do.
EYFS (Early Years Foundation Stage)
Welcome to Early Years at St Mary & All Saints: Let Our Light Shine
Welcome to the start of an extraordinary journey. At St Mary & All Saints CE Primary School, our Early Years Foundation Stage (Reception) is far more than just a classroom—it is a vibrant, welcoming launchpad where the lifelong spark of learning truly begins. We recognise that every single child arriving at our doors is an individual, overflowing with potential, wonder, and a completely unique light to shine. Our foundational mission is to cultivate a deeply safe, emotionally secure, and endlessly nurturing environment where pupils can develop the confidence and independence to make a tangible difference—to themselves, their peers, and the diverse world around them.
From their very first day, your child will be embraced by an ambitious, child-centred curriculum designed to capture their imagination and validate their unique voice. We know that children learn best when they feel safe to explore, make mistakes, and ask big questions. That is why our dedicated team of Early Years specialists works tirelessly to craft rich, memorable experiences that balance the comfort of structured routines with the thrill of open-ended discovery.
Whether your child is building complex engineering structures in our collaborative construction zones, exploring storytelling in our cosy reading corners, or conducting scientific investigations in our dynamic outdoor mud kitchens, they are constantly supported to take risks, voice their ideas, and master new skills. We are deeply committed to ensuring that school is a place of profound joy, where deep friendships are forged and where every child is seen, heard, and valued for exactly who they are.
How We Learn: Our Environment & Curriculum
We follow the statutory Early Years Foundation Stage Framework, carefully balancing child-led exploration with expert, structured adult-led teaching.
We view both our indoor and outdoor classrooms as an "extra teacher." They are intentionally designed to offer stimulating, open-ended resources that challenge children to become highly independent learners.
The Areas of Learning and Development
Our curriculum is mapped across the distinct areas of learning outlined in the statutory framework, focusing heavily on embedding the fundamental skills first:
The Three Prime Areas
These areas are critical for igniting children’s curiosity and enthusiasm for learning, and for building their capacity to learn, form relationships, and thrive:
Communication & Language
Developing listening, attention, vocabulary, and expressive speaking skills.
Physical Development
Personal, Social & Emotional Development
Enhancing gross motor skills on our outdoor equipment and fine motor control for pencil grip and tools.
Building self-regulation, positive relationships, and a strong sense of self.
The Four Specific Areas
Through these areas, the three prime areas are strengthened, deepened, and practically applied:
Literacy
Developing a love of reading, comprehension, and early writing skills (supported by our systematic synthetic phonics programme).
Mathematics
Building deep conceptual understanding of numbers, counting, patterns, and spatial reasoning.
Understanding the World
Exploring our local community, the natural world, and different cultures, faiths, and technologies.
Expressive Arts and Design
Developing a creative voice through art, music, role-play, and imaginative design.
A Partnership for Progress
Every child's developmental journey is completely unique. From the initial Reception National Baseline Assessments onwards, our experienced teachers and Learning Support Assistants (LSAs) use continuous, high-quality observations to map out individualised "next steps" tailored specifically to your child’s strengths.
We work hand-in-hand with parents and carers, sharing milestones and information regularly. We ensure that by the time our pupils achieve their Early Learning Goals (ELGs) at the end of the summer term, they are fully prepared to step into Key Stage 1 with their light shining brightly!

pageCache.pageTitle: Our Community — St Mary & All Saints
pageCache.text:
Our Community
Letting our light shine and making a difference in everything we do.
Our School Community
At St Mary & All Saints CE Primary School, we believe it takes a whole community to educate a child. In line with our foundational vision to "Let Our Light Shine," our school does not sit in isolation—we are deeply rooted within our vibrant local area, our church network, and wider global partnerships.
We work collaboratively with parents, local residents, and organisations to create a warm, supportive, and outward-looking environment where our pupils learn the true value of making a meaningful difference to the world around them.
Our Parents & Carers
(The Home-School Partnership)
Our parent body is our most vital asset. We maintain an open-door policy and actively encourage families to be part of daily school life.
The PTA (Friends of SMAS): Our fantastic Parent-Teacher Association organises wonderful community events throughout the year—from the Summer Fair to the Christmas Fair—raising vital funds to enhance our children's school resources.
Parent Volunteers: Whether helping with reading in the classroom, sharing career insights, or accompanying us on educational trips, our parents bring invaluable energy and diverse skills into our school
The Pillars of Our Community
Our Church & Spiritual Links
As a Church of England Primary School, we cherish our deep theological, pastoral, and historical links with our local parish church.
Regular Worship: We regularly visit the church for seasonal services, including Harvest, Christmas, and Easter. Our local clergy also frequently visit the school to lead collective worship.
Values in Action: Our Christian values underpin how we treat our neighbours, teaching our children the importance of community care, charity, and mutual respect.
Local & Global Partnerships
We encourage our pupils to be active global citizens who understand that they have a voice and a role to play in society.
Community Outreach: Our school choir regularly performs at local events, and our pupils take part in local environmental initiatives such as neighbourhood litter picks.
Charitable Giving: Our School Council leads termly fundraising events for both local Buckinghamshire charities and global relief efforts, empowering children to see the tangible impact of their kindness.
Class Community Action Projects
Project Spotlight: Year 1 Intergenerational Storytelling
As part of their community project, our Year 1 classes (Garnet and Emerald) have been building wonderful intergenerational friendships with the elderly residents at Beaconsfield Heights Care Home.
The children visited the care home across two separate afternoons to read aloud and share their recent story-writing projects. This beautiful initiative not only boosted the children's reading confidence and communication skills, but brought immense joy, smiles, and meaningful connection to the residents.
Community Noticeboard & Room Hire
Hosting Local Groups
Our school facilities are regularly utilised by local community groups, sports clubs, and weekend children's activities, making St Mary & All Saints a true hub of local life.
Facility Lettings
If you are a local community organisation or sports team interested in hiring our school hall, fields, or facilities, please contact the School Business Manager.

pageCache.pageTitle: Our Ethos & Christian Distinctiveness — St Mary & All Saints
pageCache.text:
Our Ethos & Christian Distinctiveness
Letting our light shine and making a difference in everything we do.
Our Ethos & Christian Distinctiveness
At St Mary & All Saints, our Christian character is the foundation of everything we do. As a Church of England school, our heritage shapes our environment, guides our relationships, and inspires our high academic ambitions. We are a living, breathing community where timeless values meet modern education.
Our daily life is guided by our core promise: "Let our Light Shine, Make a Difference."
Deeply Christian, Warmly Inclusive
Following the example of Jesus, hospitality and welcome are at the heart of who we are. We believe that every individual—pupil, staff member, and family—is unique, special, and brings something truly valuable to our school.
Because of this, our Christian character does not exclude. Instead, it creates a deeply inclusive family where children and adults of all faiths, backgrounds, and beliefs are cherished, respected, and given the space to flourish together.
Living Our Motto: "Let Your Light Shine"
We believe our first duty is to help children discover their unique talents, strengths, and passions. By nurturing their personal, emotional, and spiritual growth, we build resilient, confident individuals who are encouraged to share their unique strengths with the world.
Making a Difference: Our School Rules
To help every child feel safe, valued, and ready to learn, our daily behavior and mutual care are anchored by three simple, positive school rules that reflect our core values:
Be Kind: We look after one another, show empathy, and treat everyone with gentle consideration.
Be Respectful: We value everyone’s voice, look after our environment, and celebrate our differences.
Do Your Best: We embrace challenges with curiosity and resilience, always striving to reach our full potential.
Courageous Advocacy
Our values call us to look outward, love our neighbors, and serve others. Through community partnerships and social action, our pupils learn to speak up for fairness, care for the environment, and make a tangible, positive difference in the wider world.
Our Parish Partnership
Our school identity is strengthened by our deep, active partnerships with our local churches, St Mary & All Saints and St Michael and All Angels.
We regularly welcome local clergy into our school to enrich our assemblies and collective reflections, and our school family journeys to our church buildings to celebrate major festivals throughout the year. Through reflection, joyful song, and a commitment to service, we strive daily to be a beacon of hope and light within our community.

pageCache.pageTitle: Pastoral Support — St Mary & All Saints
pageCache.text:
Pastoral Support: Nurturing the Whole Child
Letting our light shine and making a difference in everything we do.
At St Mary & All Saints, we believe that emotional well-being and academic achievement go hand-in-hand. For a child to truly let their unique light shine, they must first feel safe, valued, understood, and happy.
Guided by our core values of Kindness and Respect, our dedicated staff work tirelessly to create a deeply supportive environment. We understand that life can bring challenges, and we are committed to building your child's Resilience so they can navigate ups and downs with confidence.
What is Pastoral Support?
Pastoral support is the emotional and social care we wrap around our pupils. It is not a "one-size-fits-all" system; instead, it is a fluid web of care tailored to each individual child.
We provide guidance, a listening ear, and targeted support for children who may be experiencing:
Anxiety, stress, or school worries.
Difficulties with friendships, social skills, or self-esteem.
Big life changes, such as bereavement, family separation, or moving house.
Challenges with emotional regulation or managing big feelings.
Our Multi-Tiered Approach to Well-being
To ensure every child receives the right care at the right time, we structure our pastoral care into three clear tiers:
Tier 1: Whole-School Care (Universal)
Every single child benefits from our strong classroom cultures. Class teachers and learning support assistants build deep relationships with pupils, checking in daily. Our inclusive PSHE curriculum, collective worships, and focus on our core Christian values ensure well-being is woven into everything we do.
Tier 2: Short-Term Targeted Support (Internal)
If a teacher or parent notices a child is struggling, we intervene early. This might include small-group friendship interventions, lunchtime check-ins, mentoring with a trusted member of staff, or structured sessions focused on building self-esteem and resilience.
A Partnership with Families
We know that you know your child best. We aim to work in absolute harmony with parents and carers. If there is a change at home—even something small—that might impact your child’s emotional state during the school day, we always encourage you to let us know so we can keep an extra, gentle eye on them.
Tier 3: Specialised External Support (Targeted)
Where a child requires deeper emotional or psychological care, we work collaboratively with families to refer to external specialists. This includes close liaison with the Specialist Teacher Service, Child and Adolescent Mental Health Services (CAMHS), and local family support charities.
How to Access Support
If you have any worries about your child's emotional or social well-being, getting help is simple:
Talk to the Class Teacher: Your child's class teacher is always the first point of contact. You can grab them briefly at the end of the day or message the office to arrange a quiet phone call.
Escalating Support: If further support is needed, the class teacher will liaise directly with our Senior Leadership Team and SENDCo, Mrs Levin, to map out a targeted pastoral plan.
If you wish to speak to someone in confidence regarding a sensitive family matter, please contact the school office directly:
Email:office@stmaryallsaints.co.uk
Telephone: 01494 673762
A Note on Safeguarding: Our pastoral care is intrinsically linked with our safeguarding practices. If any disclosure or observation indicates a child may be at risk of harm, our strict Child Protection procedures are always followed instantly to keep the child safe.

pageCache.pageTitle: Secondary Admissions & 11+ — St Mary & All Saints
pageCache.text:
Secondary Admissions & 11+
Letting our light shine and making a difference in everything we do.
Choosing the right school for your child is one of the most important decisions you will make. At St Mary & All Saints CE Primary School, we provide a nurturing, high-quality, and inspiring educational environment where every child is encouraged to let their unique light shine. Click Here
Whether your child is taking their very first steps into primary school or joining us later in their educational journey, we are here to guide you through the application process with Kindness and clarity. Click Here
Reading about our school is a wonderful start, but experiencing the warmth, energy, and vibrant learning atmosphere of St Mary & All Saints in person is truly the best way to get to know us. We love welcoming prospective families to show you how our children let their lights shine every day. Click Here
Secondary Admissions & The 11+ Process
As our pupils grow in Resilience and Curiosity, we work hard to prepare them for the next exciting chapter of their education. The transition to secondary school is a major milestone, and we are committed to supporting both our pupils and their families every step of the way.
The Buckinghamshire 11+ Selection Process
Living in Buckinghamshire, children have the opportunity to take the Transfer Test (11+) in the Autumn Term of Year 6 to determine eligibility for a grammar school place.
Preparation & Support: In line with local authority guidelines, we ensure all Year 5 children are registered for the test automatically (unless parents choose to opt-out). We provide familiarisation sessions in school to ensure children feel confident, calm, and prepared.
The Test: The practice and actual Transfer Tests take place during the first few weeks of the Autumn Term in Year 6.
Results: Results are typically released in mid-October, allowing families to make informed decisions before the secondary school application deadline.
For comprehensive details on the Transfer Test timeline, registration, and familiarisation materials, please visit the Buckinghamshire Council Transfer Test Information Page
Choosing and Applying for a Secondary School
The window for choosing a secondary school opens in September and closes at the end of October during your child's Year 6 year.
Research: Attend secondary school open evenings during September and October.
Preferences: You can list up to six secondary school preferences on your local authority application form.
National Offer Day: National Secondary Offer Day takes place on 1st March (or the next working day), when your child's allocated secondary school is revealed.
Our Promise: We maintain excellent partnerships with all local secondary schools—both upper/comprehensive and grammar schools. Once places are allocated, we host extensive transition projects and coordinate closely with secondary staff to ensure a seamless, happy move for every child.
